name: Recover an interrupted dpkg
summary: Finishes package installations that were interrupted (dpkg --configure -a) and, optionally, completes missing dependencies, without ever deleting lock files or removing packages.
risk_note: Packages left half-configured are configured now, which runs their maintainer scripts and can restart the services they provide. Where a package's configuration file was changed locally, the local version is kept. If another package operation is running, the remediation waits and then gives up instead of breaking its lock; if fixing dependencies would remove a package, it stops and says so.

linux: Waits (up to the time you choose) for any running dpkg, apt or unattended-upgrades to finish. Lock files are never deleted.
Runs dpkg --configure -a, keeping locally modified configuration files (--force-confdef --force-confold).
If that option is on, runs apt-get -f install with --no-remove, so missing dependencies are installed but no package is ever removed.
Reports dpkg --audit before and after. Does nothing where dpkg is not installed.

parameters.name: wait_seconds
parameters.label: Wait this long for a running package operation (seconds)

parameters.name: fix_dependencies
parameters.label: Also install missing dependencies (never removes packages)
